Theme

Money, work & business

accountant noun

also bookkeeper, accounts clerk, reckoner, auditor

classical

Cic. Att. 1.12.2 (Lewis & Short)
Col. 3.3.7 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 163
Traupman 268

ratiōcinātor, ratiōcinātōris m.

noun, third declension

an accountant, a reckoner

Cicero also uses it of anyone good at reckoning: ut bonī ratiōcinātōrēs esse possīmus (Off. 1.59).

Other words

  • ratiōnārius, ratiōnāriī m.

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · Traupman 163

    Not found in Lewis & Short in this sense.

  • āctuārius, āctuāriī m. — a clerk, shorthand writer; in Traupman, bookkeeper

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Suet. Caes. 55 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 164

  • ratiōcinātrīx, ratiōcinātrīcis f. — a woman accountant

    noun, third declension · also used · modern · Traupman 268

    Formed on ratiōcinātor; not in Lewis & Short.

See also accounts, calculator.
